data.title: Intuitive Surgical (ISRG) Beats In Q3 As Investors Weigh Whether The Story Still Looks Cheap
data.description:
Intuitive Surgical (ISRG) drew fresh attention after reporting third quarter 2026 results that topped analyst earnings and revenue estimates, while a sizable litigation charge pulled reported profit figures in a different direction.

The latest report landed against a tougher tape for Intuitive Surgical, with the share price down about 10% over the past week and roughly 29% year to date. This comes even as three year total shareholder return of about 25% and five year total shareholder return of about 21% point to a much stronger longer run story.

Scan beyond Intuitive Surgical and identify other robotics and automation players that options traders and analysts may be watching with our curated 90 robotics and automation stocks.

After a drop of nearly 30% this year even as long term returns remain positive, the real debate on Intuitive Surgical now is simple. Has most of the upside already played out, or is investors’ patience still being underpriced in the current valuation?

Most Popular Narrative: 37% Undervalued

On the Simply Wall St Community view, Intuitive Surgical’s fair value sits at $630.48 against a last close of $399.05, which frames the valuation gap that long term holders are debating right now. That view comes from pbco, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community, who connects Intuitive Surgical’s recurring revenue model, patent estate, and history of stock splits into a single long running investment story.

I have followed ISRG since 2003 when it was brought to the investing club I had just joined. I tried to analyze ISRG with the BetterInvesting SSG methodology that I had been introduced to and I could not get it in the buy zone. Wiser heads in the club prevailed and we started a position at around $48 a share and continued to add to the position. In 2005 ISRG was trading at over $200 a share and I was getting nervous. I convinced the club to place a trailing stop on ISRG. The price continued to increase and reached $393 a share. Then ISRG stock price started to drop it got as low as $200 a share. Our trailing stop worked like a charm we were sold out of the club position at just above $360 a share. I tried to convince the club to reinvest in ISRG at $200 a share they decided not to , but I did. I describe it as riding the lightning. I have bought and sold ISRG at least twice since then and watched the share price increase to over $1000 a share twice before doing a 3 for 1 stock split. First in 2017 and then again in 2021. Did I mention no debt?

That long memory matters because it lines up with the more formal data. Intuitive Surgical is trading at $399.05, which is about 37% below pbco’s fair value estimate of $630.48 that uses an 7.66% discount rate and bakes in revenue growth assumptions of roughly 11.47% and a profit margin of about 28.38%. The gap is large enough that the narrative does not hinge on a single quarter, but on whether the da Vinci and Ion ecosystems keep supporting that mix of margins and growth.

Result: Fair Value of $630.48 (UNDERVALUED)

Still, litigation over third party repairs and any pressure on Intuitive Surgical’s recurring instruments revenue could chip away at that long running investment case.

That kind of premium can reward patience if growth keeps justifying it, but it also raises the risk that any wobble in expectations bites harder than long term holders expect.
